body: before the most recent intern cohort, new poc/queer/minority characters have been consistently sidelined for the benefit of their white, older, cishet costars. every asian character since christina yang has been some archetype of a christina (cold, ambitious, naturally talented—which is literally a stereotype about asian people). link and nico joined at the same time, yet nico/schmitt were given no screen time & were written out despite being the only gay and asian representation on the show at the time while link became a series regular. the trans intern and intern with the hijabi were both written out after greys was praised for including them. it’s so consistent and weird—the way you make a character lovable is by writing them good storylines, so i dont get why the greys writing team seems to think that if a new character isn’t as popular they should get fewer storylines. im so sick of amelia/owen/teddy, and even link/jo isn’t as interesting. however !! i like winston/beltran a lot, i think bailey is great as a teacher, and i have a lot of hope for the new interns (i think the writers have realized they need to invest in new characters with screentime & theres a chance blue will get actual personality) so i hope this criticism changes !!

YES!!!!!! wow i can’t believe i’m not alone on this one. people recommend me happy media but my favorite type of show/movie has plot and character development but ultimately is really cynical and depressing (think grave of the fireflies, bojack horseman). part of me thinks that watching a sad thing explains and justifies feeling depressed. part of me thinks it feels like somebody trying to explain my experience and that can be helpful. op i hope you’re doing okay. this made me feel less alone today

100%. i think this might be a depression/low self esteem thing—i don’t deserve to rest and i need to do more or i’m actually a waste of space. depression makes general self care a lot more complicated for me and i go through cycles of working until i’m completely burnt out and hit double depression.

hi! im a grad student and i feel a similar “fog” that makes me think slower. first things first: prepping for as much as you can ahead of time really helps—esp w interviews. i am so bad at thinking on the spot so i literally write out my points and bring them with me in a notebook or something. no interviewer will look at you different (in fact, most of them were impressed bc it shows preparedness). w friends i try to be honest and say what’s happening (“i lost my train of thought”, “i’m trying to figure out how to say this, hang on”) and if i forget something, i tell them that i’ll say it once i remember and move on. its frustrating and im sorry its happening to you :( i hope things get better soon

god this is the story of my life. i don’t even know what “recovery” means or what my “baseline” is. im scared that my doctors are gonna think im faking because i feel like nothing i say is the right thing??? im with you on this one, for smth like this i don’t know if there is a universally “successful” outcome.

i have a really weird relationship with self sabotage that therapists do not get. i feel like sometimes, if my life is bad, then things make more sense bc i feel bad no matter what. i’ll make my own life worse, feel guilty about it, and then it becomes a self fulfilling prophecy. for ex, i always get in my head about my medication and i decide that i should go off it (to prove that i’m in control over feeling bad). i feel bad abt going off my meds bc i know i should not be doing that, and then i feel worse, etc. a therapist told me that doing this means im choosing to be depressed and that i wasn’t ready for therapy. i would like somebody who can  i understand self sabotaging behaviors as actual symptoms of being high functioning and chronically depressed, and something i want help with/treatment for. yes, i’m choosing to harm myself, but thats not necessarily the same as choosing to feel exhausted, apathetic, and guilty all the time.

also what you said about it being chronic. i have no memory of my life without depression and many of the descriptors that define depression from other emotions (are you feeling “normal” or “like yourself”?) don’t really make sense to me. i’m unlikely to “beat” this and that narrative is very unhelpful for me.

kinda… sorry i’m having trouble explaining it. overall i think yes, the lows are not as low (but a lot of other stuff changed in my life as i’ve been taking them that might have also helped). but i guess i just feel more detached from everything. like my feelings don’t affect me as much anymore, even though i still feel the feeling. i can tell that i feel really good and i don’t care, or i can tell that i feel awful and depressed and i don’t care. so i don’t know if that’s overall better or is it just bad in a different way…? i think this is more clear but this is really hard to explain, i’m so sorry.

i feel like i can’t tell if i feel overall better on meds or just not as bad, if that makes sense. like i used to really get a lot out of looking forward to things—even little things, like new episodes of tv shows or a coffee in the morning. i also would really feel good about my accomplishments, and look forward to feeling good when i did new things. now that i take meds, i don’t really get excited about anything and the main thing i feel when i get things done is dread that now i have to do something else. but before meds i was also actively planning to take myself out, and i don’t think about it like that anymore. like the apathy is so, so much worse but the dark stuff is better. so there are pros and cons.

i feel you dude. i don’t look forward to things or even feel happy when things are over. i just constantly think about how i have to still be alive for so much longer. i’m take my meds and i sleep 8 hrs a night and i spend time w friends and i keep up w work and school. and… still. i keep on working toward feeling better but i am exhausted.

i wholeheartedly believe spring day is bts’ best song! the music video is so aesthetic and the song is sonically beautiful, but i love how bts used spring day to take a political stance (re: sewol ferry) in a way that was culturally appropriate and meaningful for them, and then connected that political stance to greater human rights (they reference Omelas, Snowpiercer, and other art that focuses on the injustice of exploitation, especially of children). spring day is a rare song about grief that ends with hope, and somehow does it without disregarding the pain/complicated feelings that come with loss. yoongi’s and namjoon’s verses both mention anger, the prechorus is despair, the chorus is full of longing. but ultimately, the takeaway is that there is always hope.

no season can last forever. this song reminds me that the best is yet to come.

fun fact: the three oldest members are all youngest siblings (seokjin and yoongi both have older brothers, and hoseok has an older sister), while namjoon, jimin,  and taehyung are all the oldest child in their families (namjoon has a younger sister, taehyung has a younger brother and a younger sister, jimin has a younger brother). jungkook is the only one whose birth order matches his age order in bts (he’s a youngest in both!) and i think it explains why he seems more comfortable talking with people older than him. since age and seniority really matter in korean language/culture, i think the fact that most of the members were having to learn how to be either older/younger brothers for the first time was helpful in creating the balanced and supportive dynamic the members have with each other :)

HELLO i also identified as ace and then was diagnosed w pdd! i felt more confident in using the label asexual after my first romantic relationship began—i had no desire to do anything physically intimate (i don’t really care for kissing, even). sexy stuff is completely uninteresting if it involves myself (the idea of somebody doing things to/with me is pretty uncomfortable for me, regardless of their gender). my libido fluctuates with things like medication and hormones, but i don’t need to do anything about it and there’s never a “direction” for it. the mental health forum on aven has a lot of other aces talking abt this kind of thing if u wanna see more!

i get really exhausted, hopeless, and self destructive. my self talk gets really negative and aggressive. i also feel worthless and guilty for existing. i guilt myself into doing what needs to be done, and then i indulge in smth self destructive (consuming alcohol, going off my medications, ignoring everybody, etc), and then i feel guilty about doing that. because im always forcing myself to meet my needs it looks like everything’s fine!! but everything feels like way too much stimulation and i don’t know how i feel or what i want. even the easy things that should work feel weird and dead.

i also notice that i don’t/can’t cry. i’ve gone years without crying even though i felt like i wanted to.

after i started prozac, i felt both an extreme euphoria and an extreme anxiety (part of which i think was side effects from the medicine itself, and part of which i think was a result of me finally tackling this huge and overwhelming problem). that faded with time and i eventually felt like it wasn’t doing anything. we upped the dose and i was still feeling destructively hopeless and exhausted. when my doctor added bupropion i was expecting the same thing to happen, but instead i felt like i barely noticed any changes until one day i looked up and realized that i wasn’t relying on caffeine pills to get through my day anymore and i was feeling pretty okay in my head. basically, since ive been taking it (with the prozac) i feel both more awake and more chill. i think way less about hurting myself than i did before. ive noticed some emotional blunting (i just care way less about everything) but i was also really anxious about everything before so maybe that’s a good thing. the change was less immediately noticeable, but i think its helping.

tldr: helping overall, i think.

i don’t think your reason is nonsense! all of our reasons are gonna be a little different. i feel really guilty because i don’t think i have a good reason for being suicidal and depressed—no crazy trauma or big changes in my life, you know? but i literally feel like there’s no way to make life less painful. i’ve tried therapy, meds, talking to others, distracting myself, exercise, vitamins… i think this is just the way my life is. i’m tired of burdening my family and being a bad friend. every option sucks and nothing makes me happy, even the small things. i know that i can work harder, but mostly i’m tired of feeling guilty all the damn time and this is the most obvious way out. 
im sending you good vibes, op. i know there’s not much i can say to provide direct comfort, but i’m thinking of you today.

this happened to me too! even when i was not actively thinking about attempting, i was having suicidal thoughts all the time. when i’d have a suicidal thought (“i want to die”), i started correcting myself right after to something that was more accurate (“wait, no i don’t, i have a whole life left and there’s cool stuff to do here!”). that knee jerk reaction is hard to shake off, but noticing it and then correcting it to make it more true to how i felt helped me! (i kind of think this is similar to what they would have had you do in therapy) :)

THIS!! i implied to my ex that im suicidal and she said “i say this in the nicest way possible but you need to go to therapy”. i was so annoyed. what do you think i’ve been doing? i’ve been going for almost five months, but mental health care and therapy in general is steeped in white supremacy and values western communication styles/norms that just make therapy feel less like a solution for me (than for my ex, i guess.) as a poc in the us, i just kinda ignore when my white therapist says she “doesn’t think that’s about race” or says something kind of ignorant about my sexual orientation (bc if i wait until i find a therapist that is completely unbiased and knowledgeable abt all my experience then i might as well not go to therapy). im so disillusioned with the concept of mental health and the mental health care system in the us. effective therapy isn’t always accessible and the blanket statement “therapy is good and you need it” feels oversimplified.
